novel hybrid ceramic–metallic membrane structures were successfully prepared by deposition of a nano-structured zirconia- or titania-based sol on a porous 304L stainless steel support material.

the development of a new generation of hybrid metallic–ceramics membranes, which are expected to combine the high chemical stability of ceramic materials with the high mechanical stability of metals.
the development of a new class of ceramic–metallic hybrid membranes for potential applications in microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nano-filtration, and gas separation processes.
the preparation of new ceramic–metallic hybrid membranes with a high chemical, thermal and mechanical stability for micro-, ultra-, nano-filtration as well as for gas separation applications.

the new hybrid metallic–ceramics membranes show great potential for a wide range of applications in the field of microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nano-filtration, gas separation and pervaporation.
the new nano-structured hybrid metallic–ceramics membranes have the potential to replace polymeric membranes and current ceramic membranes for various applications.

it is feasible to manufacture hybrid ceramic–metallic membranes with an excellent chemical, thermal and mechanical stability, which are potentially suitable for a wide range of filtration and gas separation applications, including water desalination and gas purification.
